_comment: Executable ingestion policy (constitution §سادسًا). Tunable limits live HERE (never buried in code); the exit suite reads them from this file, while NON-NEGOTIABLE constants stay literal inside the validator (ق22). Versioned alongside the constitution + exit suite. NOTE: the kernel matching policy is a SEPARATE registry (engine/kernel/policyRegistry.js); unifying the two is a later, explicit decision — not Part 1.

ingestion._exclusion_note: ONLY these explicit policy categories may auto-grant signed_exclusion (path ب, still reviewable). Deliberately NO set/gift/box/pack/sample/tester patterns — those risk excluding a real sellable bundle (ق4: bundles are independent results). Any ambiguity -> merchant review queue (ق19, path أ), never auto-exclude.

surface._comment: Leaf display caps for surface_reachable (4-b): how many SKUs a leaf actually SURFACES (1 primary + N alternates). Read from policy, never hardcoded in a test — a test-written cap is an estimate, not a measure. Stamped with policy_version.

display_contract._owner: the DISPLAY / render layer (ق20) — NOT the brain. The brain READS these values; it never derives them. They are versioned WITH the display contract.
display_contract._primary_cap_note: how many PRIMARY (equally-exact) picks a DECISIVE terminal result may show (constitution: primary ≤ 3). node_kind reads it: terminal ⟺ 1 ≤ exact ≤ primary_cap; exact > primary_cap ⇒ a display GRID; exact = 0 ⇒ COMPROMISE_ONLY display. This is a DISPLAY concept, owned here — DELIBERATELY DECOUPLED from surface.leaf_primary_cap (the TREE's semantic-stop, which the FROZEN axis-selector v10 fixture depends on; ADR-0063). A value of 1 was a config error (an ‘it’, not a definition); the constitutional default is 3.
display_contract._max_published_options_note: how many options a single-select question (ق20 d*=1 one-step selector) can show. EXCEEDING it does NOT reject the axis — it ROUTES that NODE to a ق20 display mode (grid/selector). ق20 is a PER-NODE decision, not a whole-tree one.

grid._note: GAP-7 (round-10, BUILT): the oversized-leaf COMPARISON GRID. An oversized display leaf is NOT pruned — it surfaces EVERY candidate (surface = all_candidates), NO tie hidden (hide_ties=false). Declared order + a tie_break_reason per card; descriptive attributes visible on cards (PRODUCT_DECISIONS); every card's CTA is the product's real URL, authorized by the certificate (ق21) — no generic button, no fallback. This makes surface_reachable_with_grid = with_expansion, closing GAP-7.

authoring_tree._comment: Full-tree build limits (4-b). SEMANTIC stops (exact_pool<=leaf_primary_cap; no axis passes the gate) end branching for a REASON (ق12). The min_exact_option_ratio gate rejects a mostly-compromise (weakly-grounded) axis for BRANCHING — below it the axis is descriptive, not a question. The hard limits are a SAFETY NET only: exceeding them FAILS the build explicitly (never a silent truncation).
authoring_tree._v9_note: v9 (round-9): (1) the OPTIONS CAP is owned by display_contract (the brain reads it) and EXCEEDING it ROUTES the node to a ق20 display mode (grid/selector) — it no longer rejects the axis (rejecting loses legitimate information; ق20 is per-node). Likewise an ALL-SINGLETON axis routes to a display mode, not a rejection — because a product-naming was already rejected at the authoring gates, so a brain-visible all-singleton axis is a legitimate unique-per-product axis = a grid. (2) The SEMANTIC-TYPE HOMOGENEITY guard (authoring gates) is the one that catches a product-line disguised as a value (e.g. 'katana' among origins, 2 SKU/line — it escapes all three counting layers because support=2 and |values|≠|products|); mixing semantic types ⇒ reject regardless of counts. (3) The |distinct|==|grounded| gate is REPLACED by an EVIDENCE-BASIS gate: reject only when values are derived from product identity (name_token) with no independent vocabulary; a catalog-independent vocabulary (structured / variant option / taxonomy) is a real axis EVEN IF each value is unique to one product — count-equality becomes a reported signal. PERMANENT RULE: gates are relations or evidence-basis; a numeric threshold is accepted only when derived from an existing policy key OR a contract owned by non-brain — a number without a declared owner is a rejected free number.
authoring_tree._v8_note: v8 (round-8) reframes mirror as a BEHAVIORAL property (one question that isolates candidates by itself), judged in three layers, each in its right place: (1) the decisive counts bound (no published option isolates >1 item ⇒ reject) — zero false positives but LARGE false negatives on wide catalogs, so it is not the real defense; (2) max_published_options_per_question — a question with more options than one display can hold (ق20 one-step selector) is unusable regardless of classification ⇒ the axis is NOT branched (routed to a ق20 display-mode decision) and reported; (3) the authoring gates (authoring/brain2/authoringGates.js), where the VALUES are visible, as RELATIONS not ratios: basis==name_token ∧ support==1 ⇒ the value is a product NAME (dropped); |distinct values|==|grounded products| ⇒ the axis is a naming of products (rejected); value≈product title ⇒ merchant review (ق19). CORRECTED mirror denominator: mirror_singleton_share counts singletons over VALUE-CONFIRMING options only (excludes u₀ AND any 'don't care' option — both confirm no value), so a big don't-care bucket cannot mask a mirror; the ranking keeps both as real buckets. SURFACED (per the permanent rule 'no free number'): max_published_options_per_question=8 is a PROVISIONAL value derived from the ق20 one-step-selector display capacity (a mobile single-select stays scannable) — confirm/derive from the display contract. On oud it is inert (max options per axis = 5). PERMANENT RULE: every gate is a relation or evidence-basis; a gate needing a ratio/free-number is deferred until its denominator is derived from an existing contract.
authoring_tree._v7_mirror_note: v7 (round-7) reduces the mirror GUARD to the single infallible counts-only bound: reject an axis for branching ONLY when no published option isolates >1 item (max sᵢ < 2 — a disguised grid); no threshold, no small-pool exemption (a grid is always more honest). The minority-mirror case is a REPORTED signal, not a gate: mirror_singleton_share = (#singleton options)/Σsᵢ (measured on GROUNDED options only — an unknown is not a revealing option), surfaced per chosen axis (tree.mirrorSignals) and escalated to the authoring gates where the VALUES are visible (mirror is a semantic property the counts-only brain cannot judge). Two denominators kept distinct: RANKING residual = (Σsᵢ²+u₀²)/S (unknown is a real bucket); MIRROR share = /Σsᵢ (unknown is not an option). This retires the v6 Σsᵢ²/S<leaf_total_cap guard, which was doubly broken (hybrid denominator underscored sparse-grounding axes like oud `origin`; threshold contradicted leaf_primary_cap; size-weighted ⇒ blind to a minority mirror). leaf_total_cap/mirror_singleton_share_max/mirror_option_density_max are retained as v6/v5/v4 legacy only.
authoring_tree._v6_mirror_note: v6 (round-6) replaces the free-floating singleton-share (blind to all-size-2 distributions) with a DERIVED mirror metric in the score's own currency: EXPECTED RESIDUAL POOL SIZE Σsᵢ²/S. Reject an axis for branching when Σsᵢ²/S < leaf_total_cap (integer: Σsᵢ² < leaf_total_cap·S); EXEMPT when S ≤ leaf_total_cap (the whole pool already fits one display grid, so any split is at worst redundant, not a mirror). ANCHOR DEVIATION (surfaced): the operator's command said leaf_primary_cap, but leaf_primary_cap=1 makes the criterion INERT (Σsᵢ²/S ≥ 1 always) — it rejects nothing and fails the operator's own all-size-2 test; leaf_total_cap satisfies all three stated tests. Confirm. DENOMINATOR CAVEAT (surfaced, per the 'justify the denominator' rule): S includes the u₀ unknowns, so a SPARSE-but-legitimate soft axis (large u₀, e.g. oud `origin` at 58% ungrounded) is flagged as a mirror by Σsᵢ²/S although its options don't fragment (Σsᵢ²/Σsᵢ clears it). This literal-/S false-positive is SHOWN, not silently switched — operator to decide the denominator. Every mirror rejection is reported (tree.guardRejections) as an axis GATE-FAILURE signal (a product-identity axis should have failed a conceptual/grounding gate before the brain). mirror_singleton_share_max/mirror_option_density_max are retained as v5/v4 legacy only.
authoring_tree._axis_rule_note: v5 axis-selection law (consultation round-5). SCORE unchanged from v4: reduction = S - (Σsᵢ² + u₀²)/S, where S = the node's EXACT-pool size |E| (a NODE property, identical for every candidate axis at the node), sᵢ = per-option EXACT count, u₀ = S - Σsᵢ the explicit UNKNOWN-on-axis residual bucket. S node-constant ⇒ ranking by max reduction == ranking by MIN integer (Σsᵢ² + u₀²) — no division/float/log. Justification = EXPECTED RESIDUAL POOL SIZE (Σsᵢ²/S = Σ(sᵢ/S)·sᵢ), not Gini. v5 changes: (1) DENOMINATOR invariant asserted per axis per node — Σsᵢ + u₀ == S (else cross-axis comparison undefined ⇒ build fails). (2) UNKNOWN-REACHABILITY invariant (server-side verifyReachability): u₀>0 ⇒ a PUBLISHED option must lead to the u₀ units (every parent-EXACT candidate stays inside some child's eligible pool); otherwise u₀² hides a reachability loss (ق2) ⇒ build fails. (3) MIRROR guard is now PER-OPTION not distributional: reject an axis whose SINGLETON SHARE (options of size 1, as a fraction of Σsᵢ) exceeds mirror_singleton_share_max — but NOT applied when S <= leaf_primary_cap+1 (an honest final binary on a tiny pool); the v4 median/density criteria are RETIRED as rejections. Tie-break unchanged: fewer options -> smaller max sᵢ -> higher axis evidence (grounding coverage) -> canonical id (last resort).
authoring_tree._mirror_exemption_note: The mirror guard is skipped when S <= leaf_primary_cap+1. NOTE (surfaced deviation): the operator's literal 'S <= leaf_primary_cap' is redundant — with leaf_primary_cap=1 such a node is already a leaf via semantic-stop-1, so it never reaches axis selection, and it would NOT exempt the operator's own S=2 accept-case. leaf_primary_cap+1 is the final binary that narrows the pool to the cap; it exempts S=2 (two distinct products = an honest question) while a large-catalog mirror (S>>cap) is still gated. Confirm or adjust this bound.
authoring_tree._unknown_axis_handling_note: For the info-gain accounting an UNGROUNDED value on the candidate axis is a SEPARATE residual bucket u₀ (excluded from every option size sᵢ), never propagated into the options. Well-defined because an ungrounded value is NEVER `exact` (exact requires SAT requires grounded). The kernel's downstream CLASSIFICATION of such a unit stays mode-dependent and UNCHANGED (a NEVER_RELAX axis rejects it; a RELAXABLE axis compromises it into every branch) — the runtime partition, separate from this design-time accounting. v5 makes the two invariants HARD: Σsᵢ + u₀ == S (partition), and u₀>0 ⇒ published reach to the u₀ units (no silent drop of a NEVER_RELAX-ungrounded exact candidate).
